name: Senthil Kannan
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 77-year-old male college lecturer reports worsening joint stiffness and mild dyspnoea on exertion.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 78 kg, BMI 25.6 (obese). Joints tender and swollen in MCP and PIPs, no deformities. Cardiac exam: S1S2, no murmurs, mild basal crepitations. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Active rheumatoid arthritis; heart failure with reduced EF, NYHA II. Obesity noted.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue methotrexate 10 mg weekly, folic acid 5 mg weekly, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg OD, prednisolone 5 mg OD. Continue sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, spironolactone 25 mg OD, furosemide 40 mg OD, dapagliflozin 10 mg OD. Advise low‑salt diet, regular walking, weight reduction. Return if chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, or sudden joint swelling.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: ESR 32 mm/hr (0-20), CRP 12 mg/L (<5), Rheumatoid factor 48 IU/ml (<14), Anti‑CCP 210 U/ml (<20). LFT: ALT 28 U/ml (≤40), AST 26 U/ml (≤40), ALP 84 U/ml (≤120), GGT 32 U/ml (≤50), bilirubin 0.9 mg/dl (≤1.2). Lipids: Cholesterol 210 mg/dl (<200), Triglycerides 165 mg/dl (<150), HDL 38 mg/dl (>40), LDL 132 mg/dl (<100). FBS 102 mg/dl (70-100). Serum Na 138 mmol/l (135-145), K 4.6 mmol/l (3.5-5.0), Creatinine 1.1 mg/dl (0.6-1.2), eGFR 62 ml/min/1.73m2. NT‑proBNP 310 pg/ml (<125).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Echocardiogram: Left ventricular ejection fraction 38% (normal 55‑70). Left atrial size mildly enlarged. No significant valvular disease. Diastolic dysfunction grade II. Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 32 mmHg. NYHA class II.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Increased swelling of ankles over past 2 weeks, joint pain worse in mornings.
EXAMINATION: BP 142/88 mmHg, weight 80 kg, BMI 26.1 (obese). Bilateral pitting edema up to mid‑calf. Joints: tender swollen wrists, MCP joints. Cardiovascular: regular rhythm, no added sounds. Lungs: clear.
IMPRESSION: Fluid overload likely contributing to edema; RA flare.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase furosemide to 60 mg OD. Add spironolactone 25 mg BD (total 50 mg OD). Continue other HF meds. For RA, add prednisolone taper: start 10 mg OD for 5 days then reduce by 2.5 mg every 3 days to 5 mg OD. Advise low‑salt diet, elevate legs, monitor weight daily. Return if sudden weight gain >2 kg in 3 days, increased dyspnoea, chest pain, or fever.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Through clinic app: "Doctor, my hands are very stiff in the morning and I can’t grip my coffee cup. Also my feet feel swollen even after taking the extra furosemide."

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Persistent morning stiffness and ankle edema despite medication changes.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/86 mmHg, weight 79.5 kg, BMI 25.9 (obese). Mild synovitis in wrists and MCP joints. Bilateral pitting edema to ankles. Cardiac exam: regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: RA inadequately controlled; HF stable on current regimen.
ARRANGEMENTS: Refer to rheumatology for consideration of biologic agent. Continue current HF meds. Add methotrexate 15 mg weekly (increase from 10 mg). Keep folic acid. Continue hydroxychloroquine. Taper prednisolone to 5 mg OD over next week. Advise joint protection exercises, weight control. Return if worsening dyspnoea, chest pain, fever, or rapid joint swelling.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient presents for seasonal influenza vaccine.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, weight 79 kg, BMI 25.5 (obese). No acute distress.
IMPRESSION: RA and HF stable. Obesity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Administered inactivated influenza vaccine 0.5 ml IM left deltoid. Documented vaccine given today. Advise to monitor for local reaction or fever. Continue current meds. Return if chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or worsening joint pain.

memories.text: Rheumatology review received. Patient assessed, disease activity moderate (DAS28 3.8). Recommendation: Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly, add sulfasalazine 500 mg BD, consider tapering glucocorticoids. No biologic indicated at present due to comorbidities. Return rheumatology review to primary care.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine follow‑up; reports good energy, occasional mild joint stiffness.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/78 mmHg, weight 77.5 kg, BMI 24.9 (overweight). No joint swelling or tenderness. No edema. Cardiac exam regular, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: RA in low disease activity; HF compensated; overweight.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Advise maintain weight <23 BMI through diet and regular activity. Return if chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or new joint swelling.
